about: An underground-empire dungeon in the Zork style. I start at an endless stair on a final test set by a silver-haired old man. I explore a cavern network: a cliff with a rope, a shadow land with a hooded swordsman, a freezing lake, a grue-filled dark passage, and a rusted iron door.

done.why: I died to grues in the dark passage south of the lake and was sent back to the start. I had seen most reachable rooms and could not get past the locked chest, the rusted door, the rubble or the dark, so I stopped.

ending.what: No ending. I died in the grue lair and the old man revived me at the Endless Stair, with my gear scattered along the way in.

moments.note: Someone is watching from above the cliff. The rope twitches and they chuckle. The chest is locked.
I scrambled down the cliff and could not go back up. That cut me off from the chest and the watcher.
The lake instructions were clear. I dropped my gear on the shore, swam, and found a golden amulet on the bottom.
The diagonal exits in the shadow land were hard to map.
The grues killed me even though I was wearing the amulet.

wished: Reach the person at the top of the rope, or open the locked chest. I climbed down before trying and could not go back up.
Get past the grue passage, the rusted door and the rubble.
Spare the hooded figure rather than kill it. I only noticed the hint (the hood within reach) after it vanished.

lines.line: It fights the way you fight, and no better, and no worse: wounded, you are slower, and so is it.
lines.why: It teaches the combat rule and tells you that retreat is allowed.

lines.line: The light you carry throws your shadow on the water, which does not want it.
lines.why: It gives a clear hint for the lake puzzle in a good voice.

lines.line: Oh, no! Dozens of lurking grues attack and devour you!
lines.why: The death, followed by the old man's revival scene.

fun.why: Exploring was pleasant and the lake and the duel were good. Being blocked by the dark and the locked things, then killed, was frustrating.

engagement.why: The unseen watcher and the small mysteries kept me going. The confusing direction names in the shadow land slowed me down.

difficulty.why: Several routes were blocked with no clear way forward, and the grue dark killed me with no warning that the amulet would not help.

interestingness.why: The watcher at the rope, the engravings, the hooded figure and the dream framing all point to a larger story.

prose.why: The prose is atmospheric, and the extra hint lines for the lake and the aqueduct are well written.
